card.summary: Upload once and the file is mirrored to the hosts the user selects, yielding one aggregate link; 'Over 40 hosts to choose from'.

free_tier.stated: Upload once and the file is mirrored to the hosts the user selects, yielding one aggregate link; 'Over 40 hosts to choose from'.
free_tier.notes: No free allowance is printed; the free product is the service itself.

per_object_cap.stated: not stated on the page read

retention.stated: not applicable: the copies live on the destination hosts, under each host's own retention

egress.terms: Downloads come from the destination hosts, so their limits apply, not Mirrorcreator's. The service itself publishes no byte allowance and no price.

record.interface_detail: Web form. The site names Google Drive, Mediafire, GoFile, Yandex Disk among the 40+ destinations, and states 'The files you upload are stored on your own accounts on hosting sites'.
record.tooling: Browser only as read. No API found on the page; a wrapper would have to drive the form per host.
record.chaining: The inverse of a debrid: instead of pulling one link from many hosts, it pushes one file to many hosts.

limits.value: unstated; the service bounds a run by the number of selected destinations

record.limits_note: Uploading into the user's own accounts means the destination host's quota, not Mirrorcreator's, is what runs out first. Anonymous destinations avoid that at the cost of the files being outside the account's control.
record.binding_note: Mirrorcreator stores nothing itself, so no byte counter of its own can bind at 1 TiB. The constraint moves to whichever destination host is selected.

identity_cost.detail: Uploads can be anonymous where a destination allows it, or made into the user's own accounts ('if the hosting sites support anonymous file uploads, you can even upload files without the need for registration'). No Mirrorcreator account was required on the page read.

record.reliability_note: An aggregate link is only as alive as the destinations behind it; when one host removes a file the aggregate page keeps listing a dead mirror until somebody clicks it.
record.confidence_note: The 40+ host claim, the own-account behaviour and the aggregate-link behaviour are read from the vendor page. Nothing was uploaded.

evidence.proved: 'Over 40 hosts to choose from', 'The files you upload are stored on your own accounts on hosting sites', and the example destinations Google Drive, Mediafire, GoFile, Yandex Disk

record.price_per_tb_month: USD 0, plus the destination host's own cost
record.notes: The domain is mirrored.to but the site brands itself Mirrorcreator, the older name; MirrorAce is a separate site on the same idea and is recorded dead.
